task.description: WF-03 Step 1: independently re-verify ISS-0424's own measured R-Co-mention counts, confirm the pin_rebind.ex hardcoded path, and recommend a concrete 3-part split (framing / parity-justifications / provenance) with a to_agent routing decision, following the ISS-0425 -> REQ-219/REQ-220 precedent for how an architectural issue gets decomposed into requirements.

result.summary:
RE-VERIFICATION (independent grep, this run, excluding .git/deps/_build/node_modules; web/node_modules does not exist as a separate excludable path -- no such directory found, so no extra exclusion was needed):

1. Total 'R-Co' occurrences repo-wide: 6070 (grep -roI 'R-Co' | wc -l) -- EXACTLY matches the issue's filed count. Files touched: 849 (grep -rlI, this run) vs the issue's claimed 870 -- close but not identical; the ~2% gap is attributable to grep-pattern/exclusion differences (e.g. this run used -I to skip binaries) rather than a wrong order of magnitude. Verdict: the scale claim (thousands of mentions, hundreds of files) is CONFIRMED, exact digit is not load-bearing for sizing.

2. '.zig' provenance citations: the issue's ~1235 does not reproduce under an '.zig' occurrence count (4316 raw occurrences of the substring '.zig') nor under 'lines containing both R-Co and .zig' (906 lines). Both of my independent countings are in the same order of magnitude as ~1235 (906 is the closer proxy; 4316 overcounts because some moduledocs list several .zig paths per R-Co-mentioning paragraph without repeating the word 'R-Co' on every line, e.g. lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:57-58 has two .zig citations on consecutive lines sharing one 'R-Co' mention). CONFIRMED: several hundred to low-thousands of provenance citations exist; the issue's own ~1235 is a defensible middle estimate, not independently exactly reproduced by either of my two grep proxies. This does not change the sizing conclusion -- provenance citations are numerous and wide regardless of which of the three estimates (906 / 1235 / 4316) is used.

3. Deliberate-divergence notes: grepping the phrasing actually used in the tree ('unlike R-Co', 'deliberately diverges', 'diverges from R-Co' -- confirmed real phrasing via lib/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex:11, lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md:420, lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md:428) yields 49 lines repo-wide, vs the issue's claimed 38. The issue's 38 is likely scoped to lib/ production code only (excluding lib/letflow/design/*.md, which carries several of the 49 -- e.g. req194, req021, req219 design docs above are NOT production code). CONFIRMED as the right order of magnitude and the right phrasing family; recommend PARITY-JUSTIFICATIONS and PROVENANCE work exclude these lines by the same phrase-family grep before touching any file, regardless of whether the count is exactly 38 or 49.

4. Parity-justification phrasing in lib/ (excluding lib/letflow/design/): grep for 'matches R-Co|mirrors R-Co|same as R-Co|R-Co.s own|R-Co own|parity|port of R-Co' in lib/ gives 148 occurrences across 52 files (this run), vs the issue's 131/47. Close enough to confirm both the phrase family and the rough scale; the issue's narrower count likely applied additional judgement filtering (e.g. excluding 'parity' where used in an unrelated sense, or excluding lib/mix/tasks/). File breakdown by subsystem (this run, 52 files): routers 12, engine 7, definitions 6, event_store 3, engine/wasm 3, plugs 2, lib/mix/tasks 2, engine/lua 2, api 2, and 1 each in webhooks, tenant_provisioning.ex, tasks.ex, sandbox_pool, repository, instances.ex, identity.ex, identity/, event_store/registry, event_store.ex, engine.ex, definitions.ex, audit.ex.

5. pin_rebind.ex CONFIRMED: lib/letflow/engine/pin_rebind.ex line 8 reads (moduledoc): 'c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co is reachable, and REQ-110 read' -- an absolute Windows filesystem path to the R-Co source tree, hardcoded in production moduledoc prose (not executable code, not a config value, no test asserts on it). This matches the issue's own claim of exactly one such occurrence; I did not find a second one while reading nearby lines or in the grep passes above (no other 'c:\\Users' hits surfaced in the R-Co grep output sampled).

SPLIT RECOMMENDATION (per ORCHESTRATOR.md #10's six-check sizing rule, applied per part, and following the ISS-0425 -> REQ-219/REQ-220 precedent of a REQ-ANALYST-drafted decomposition for a wide architectural issue):

PART 1 -- FRAMING (CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/migration/README.md): touches 3 files, so it fails check 1 of the six-check test ('exactly one file') as a single action, but each individual file edit independently passes all six checks (no new public function/module/spec, no migration, no supervision-tree file, no tenant-data path, no test asserts on this prose). RECOMMEND: ORCH performs this as THREE separate direct-action edits (one per file, one PR each or one PR touching all three with per-file direct-action reasoning noted -- ORCH's call), no REQ-ANALYST/CODE-DESIGNER pipeline needed. This is the one part of the three that does NOT need a requirement.

PART 2 -- PARITY-JUSTIFICATIONS (131-148 occurrences, 47-52 files, lib/ production code, judgement-call rewrites): FAILS the sizing rule outright (many files, and per the issue's own text explicitly NOT mechanical -- each rewrite is a judgement call about what to keep/restate/delete, which is exactly the kind of design decision the direct-action exception exists to exclude). This needs a REQ-ANALYST-drafted requirement, almost certainly more than one given the ISS-0425 precedent (REQ-219 + dependent REQ-220 for a follow-on sweep). RECOMMENDED CHUNKING by subsystem, sized similarly to how REQ-219/REQ-220 split (a primary requirement plus dependent follow-ups): (a) routers (12 files) -- largest single cluster, likely its own requirement; (b) engine + engine/wasm + engine/lua (7+3+2=12 files) -- one requirement, natural grouping since these already share design docs under lib/letflow/design/req0*-*.md; (c) definitions + definitions.ex (7 files); (d) event_store + event_store.ex + event_store/registry (5 files); (e) remainder -- plugs, api, webhooks, tenant_provisioning, tasks, sandbox_pool, repository, instances, identity(+dir), engine.ex, audit.ex, lib/mix/tasks (approx 14 files) -- one requirement or split again if REQ-VALIDATOR judges it too wide. Each requirement's acceptance criteria should require per-occurrence judgement (keep/restate/delete) rather than a blanket rule, and explicitly exclude the 38-49 deliberate-divergence lines (which are OUT OF SCOPE per the issue) by the same phrase-family grep used above.

PART 3 -- PROVENANCE (.zig citations, ~900-4300 lines depending on counting method, wide but issue says 'mechanical-ish'): FAILS the sizing rule (touches far more than one file, and spans lib/, docs/migration/, and design docs). Unlike Part 2 this is closer to mechanical (demote existing citations to a consistent marked-provenance convention) but still needs a CODE-DESIGNER-level decision on what the convention actually is (e.g. a heading/prefix format) before any file is touched, and the issue itself does not specify one. RECOMMEND: one REQ-ANALYST requirement to (i) define the provenance-marking convention (design decision, likely delegated to CODE-DESIGNER once the requirement exists) and (ii) apply it, chunked by directory/subsystem the same way as Part 2 if a single ELIXIR-DEV/FRONTEND-DEV turn proves too large once the convention is fixed -- this requirement should explicitly depend_on or sequence after Part 2's requirement(s) for any file that appears in both (a parity-justification rewrite and a provenance citation in the same file should not be two uncoordinated edits landing out of order).

ROUTING: this diagnosis routes to REQ-ANALYST (not directly to ORCH for a WF-03 CODE-DESIGNER handoff), because Parts 2 and 3 are not 'fix an existing specified behavior' work (WF-03's normal shape) -- they are new-requirement-shaped work needing docs/requirements.yaml entries with their own acceptance criteria, exactly as ISS-0425 was handled. Part 1 does not need a requirement; ORCH can pick that up directly as three single-file direct-action edits at any point without waiting on REQ-ANALYST. Recommend REQ-ANALYST draft REQ IDs for Parts 2 (chunked, likely 3-5 requirements per the subsystem grouping above) and 3 (1 requirement for the convention + design, or 1 primary + dependents mirroring REQ-219/REQ-220 if the applied-citation sweep proves too large for one ELIXIR-DEV turn), then route through REQ-VALIDATOR and WF-02 as normal. No fix was implemented in this step; this is diagnosis/sizing only per WF-03 Step 1's own scope.
